data.hypothesis: Loading each source particle once into block-shared memory and reusing it across target threads may reduce repeated global source loads. The pairwise arithmetic and source iteration order remain unchanged, isolating memory reuse; barriers and bounds checks cover partial tiles and inactive target threads.
data.notes: The 256-particle static shared-memory tile matches the supplied 256-thread block configuration. Every thread follows the same tile loop and reaches both barriers, including threads beyond n. Mass is copied unchanged from the input particle. Correctness and timing remain for the controller to evaluate; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Stage source particles cooperatively in a 256-entry static shared-memory tile and reuse each tile across the block's target rows.
Keep inactive target threads in the uniform tile/barrier loop and guard both source loads and output writes for partial blocks.
Preserve source iteration order, force arithmetic, and the input particle mass when forming each output.
